provenance.how: constructed from the ADR's literals at the pinned ref and cross-checked against the core's own builders (tests/unit/mobile/test_push_wire_contract.py); not captured from a running relay, because no relay route emits the machine-side shapes yet

sound_values.default: the computer's `system` choice: the phone plays its OS default notification sound (iOS aps.sound = "default"; Android sound.default)
sound_values.none: notifications.sound.enabled is false on the computer: the banner posts silently (iOS omits aps.sound; Android uses the silent sound.none channel)
sound_values.fallback: soft-pulse — any computer selection that is not a built-in (a custom sound, or a hand-edited id that names nothing) sends soft-pulse in data.sound, because a phone that does not hold the custom file must still play the default rather than an OS sound; the custom file travels by name in the reserved, optional sound_custom (not sent yet)
sound_values.custom: c_<sha256[:16]> (lowercase hex; custom_pattern) — RESERVED, carried only by the optional sound_custom (not by sound), only when the selection is a custom sound and enabled is true; not sent yet

notes: THE ROUTE IS THE FROZEN ONE and there is no second spelling: the devices block rides a call that already exists rather than a route of its own.
The body IS the payload object plus the devices block (the registration forward and the heartbeat carry the same block; their routes are cloud-side proposals).

alert is COMPOSED BY THE MACHINE and delivered verbatim by the cloud, for every type (the lane's ruling of 2026-10-01): the title is APP_NAME and the body is a house constant for the kind plus the count — here BODY_COMPLETE and count 2. It is the only place a title or a body may appear anywhere in a push, and its text is never a conversation name, a transcript snippet or a provider's error line.

The count in the body is §3.2's count — the machine's unread CONVERSATION count at composition time, the same number S1's badge counts — which is why the sentence says conversations and never updates.

ONE NUMBER, ONE NOUN, AND THE NOUN AGREES WITH THE NUMBER: the body's count term is `<n> conversation(s) need(s) you`, so a count of one reads `1 conversation needs you` rather than `1 conversations need you` — a count of one being the common case for a completion push. alert_count_one files that literal so no reader of this tree only ever sees the plural; the ruling note carries the amendment.
conversation is the per-machine opaque handle (S2), never a session id, and it is what makes apns-collapse-id / notification.tag collapse per conversation.
kind is the STORE's vocabulary — complete, error, interrupted, closed, retired — not the composer's set, which is missing 'closed'.
count is the machine's unread count at composition time: the one aggregate the design discloses to the cloud on purpose.

emit_id is the machine's identity for one emit (dedupe, and the cloud's delivery record). It replaces the revision counters the earlier draft carried — an opaque uuid cannot be read as activity volume.
There is no aps envelope and no badge here: what the phone receives is the cloud's fan-out, and aps.badge is never sent (payload-forbidden-fields.json).

sound is the computer's selected notification sound, MAPPED by the cloud and never composed from (notification-sounds design §3.6, ADR 0006 amendment), per value. iOS: a built-in id → aps.sound = "<id with - → _>.wav" (e.g. "soft_pulse.wav": the bundled file name, because Android res/raw names must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and expo-notifications applies one sounds: list to both platforms; data.sound itself still carries the catalog id); "default" → aps.sound = "default" (the OS default sound); "none" → aps.sound OMITTED (an unknown file name would make APNs play the default sound, the opposite of the setting). Android: android.channel_id = "sound.<id>" for a built-in, "sound.default" for default, and the silent "sound.none" channel for none (a channel's sound is fixed at creation). A custom selection, or any id the phone has no file for, sends soft-pulse (the phone may not hold the custom file; sound_custom, reserved below, names it for a device that does); notifications.sound.enabled false sends none. The computer's volume does not travel: the phone plays at its own notification volume. sound_values lists every value the field may carry.

sound_custom and devices[].sound_custom_ready are RESERVED, OPTIONAL and NOT SENT YET (ADR 0006 amendment 2026-11-04; notification-sounds addendum 2 §2.2): the phone will fetch the computer's custom sound through the tunnel and cache it, and the cloud picks PER DEVICE — sound_custom_ready true → iOS aps.sound = "<sound_custom>.wav", Android channel_id = "sound.<sound_custom>"; otherwise it maps data.sound exactly as above, which stays required and still carries soft-pulse for a custom selection. sound_custom is "c_<sha256[:16]>" of the stored WAV, lowercase hex, matching sound_values.custom_pattern ^c_[0-9a-f]{16}$ (the cloud validates the SHAPE, not only the type, because it splices the value into aps.sound and an Android channel id), never the user's sound name, so P2 holds; the underscore makes the wire value the phone's file stem (c_<sha16>.wav), so there is no second mapping. They are declared now because the cloud validates with extra="forbid": reserving them before S7 builds avoids a cloud-first deploy when core's notification-sounds C5 starts emitting them. reserved_not_sent lists them, and the suite asserts today's builder output carries neither.
